newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Fate of Venezuelan airline to be settled this week.
newsitem.headline: Fate of Venezuelan airline to be settled this week.

text.p: The future of troubled Venezuelan airline Viasa will be decided on Friday when shareholders are expected to vote on whether to declare the country's flag carrier bankrupt, company sources said on Tuesday.
Viasa grounded all its planes on Thursday, stranding hundreds of passengers, and its executive board originally set the extraordinary shareholders' meeting for Feb. 8.
"The meeting has been brought forward due to the grave emergency," one company source told Reuters.
"Waiting 15 days until February 8 was too long," Viasa commercial director Juan Pedro Aritio told the local daily newspaper El Universal.

Viasa's long-standing difficulties worsened earlier this month when workers overwhelmingly rejected an emergency cost-cutting plan, said to be the last attempt to save the partly Spanish-owned airline from bankruptcy.

Venezuela's National Investment Fund President Alberto Poletto, with portfolio for privatisations, was in Madrid on Tuesday for a second day of talks with the Spanish government to try and save the airline.
State-owned Spanish carrier Iberia holds the largest stake in Viasa with 45 percent, Venezuela has a 40 percent share and Venezuela's largest bank, Banco Provincial, owns 15 percent.
Viasa, which employs about 2,200 people and was founded 35 years ago, registered a $30 million loss last year and has not reported a profit since Iberia took over management in 1991.
